findings.evidence: The form's heading states 'Set up your account' but requires fields like company website, membership number, account number, organization name, shipping speed, and contact time that are not needed to create an account.
findings.fix: Remove unnecessary fields or make them optional. Ask for company website, shipping preferences, contact time, and other secondary details after account creation or in a separate account preferences step.
findings.violation: The form asks for unnecessary fields for the stated task of account setup: company website, membership number, account number, organization name, shipping speed, and contact time could be asked later or omitted. Additionally, the form asks for the person's name twice: once as a full name field and again as separate first and last name fields.

findings.fix: Say beside the field what the number is used for, or make it optional.
findings.violation: A phone number is required with no word beside the field on why it is needed, though the form already asks for an email address.

findings.fix: Move the rule into hint text beside the field, linked with aria-describedby.
findings.violation: A format rule appears only in the placeholder, which disappears as soon as typing starts.

findings.fix: Mark the optional fields with the word optional in their labels, or mark the required ones and explain the mark.

instances.evidence: <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="password-input" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" required="" minlength="6">
<input id="street-input" name="street_address" type="text" autocomplete="address-line1" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">
<input id="given-input" name="given_name" type="text" autocomplete="given-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="family-input" name="family_name" type="text" autocomplete="family-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">

findings.violation: The form mixes 14 required and 1 optional fields and marks none of them, so the person cannot tell which may be left empty.
A control that clears everything entered sits directly beside the submit button.

findings.fix: Increase the button size to at least 44 CSS pixels in both dimensions. Use padding of at least 8 to 10 pixels and a larger font size.
findings.violation: The View details button is far too small to tap accurately on a mobile device. It declares padding of 1px 2px and font-size of 11px, making it well below the 44-pixel recommended size for touch targets.
This account number is a text field without the numeric input mode, so a phone shows the full keyboard for digits.

findings.fix: Offer the options as visible radio buttons.
findings.violation: A single choice among 3 options sits in a drop-down, so the person must open it to see them.

findings.evidence: <input id="password-input" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" required="" minlength="6">
findings.fix: Require at least eight characters and remove the pattern and any maximum length.
findings.violation: On this new-password field, the minimum length is only 6.

findings.evidence: <input id="given-input" name="given_name" type="text" autocomplete="given-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required=""> <input id="family-input" name="family_name" type="text" autocomplete="family-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
findings.fix: Collect the name in one field.
findings.violation: One name is split across 2 fields, so the person moves between boxes for a single value.
